newsitem.title: FRANCE: EUROTUNNEL SEES 50/50 CHANCE OF LICENCE EXTENSION.
newsitem.headline: EUROTUNNEL SEES 50/50 CHANCE OF LICENCE EXTENSION.

text.p: Eurotunnel SA /Plc chief executive Patrik Ponsolle said on Thursday he saw a one in two chance of getting an extension to its concession for operating the Channel Tunnel.

"There is one chance in two as one government has said it is in favour and the second has not said 'no,' he said at the presentation of Eurotunnel's prospectus for its 70-billion franc debt restructuring.
The new British Labour government has just taken office and France is holding a parliamentary election, in which a second ballot will be held on June 1.

An extension of the concession, currently 65 years, would allow lower depreciation charges, an earlier return to profit and dividend payment and a larger share of the equity for holders of the 2001 warrants, Ponsolle said.
France has indicated it wants an extension to the licence, which would help gain shareholder approval for the restructuring plan.
